summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable sticky directory. Live tests before and after reboot confirmed users can create and delete their own files but cannot delete files owned by another user. RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were retained.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop with root:root ownership and mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt).
Verified behavior using two unprivileged UIDs: both created files, cross-user deletion was denied, and owner deletion succeeded.
Safely restarted node1 and confirmed its boot ID changed.
Repeated permission and behavioral checks after restart; cleaned up all test files.

evidence.requirement: Shared writable directory with protection against deleting other users' files
evidence.summary: Shows /srv/drop as root:root mode 1777 and proves live two-user behavior: both users wrote files, cross-user deletion failed with Operation not permitted, and owners deleted their own files.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence reports RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64.

Captures healthy baseline behavior, restart acknowledgement with old boot ID 5f3ce3b8-4860-447e-bcf1-d6643718694e, reachable system with changed boot ID e2922551-5292-4b0b-b8c6-4c2b2d26a3c0, and full post-restart directory and access-behavior recovery.
